body.p: Use to send your commits to the remote repository. Use to download commits from the remote repository and update your local branch.

section.title: Push Changes
section.p: On Git Staging, select to send your local commits to the remote repository.
If the remote branch has commits that you do not have locally, the push fails. Pull first to update your local branch, then push again.

fig.title: Push Error When Local Branch Is Behind

p.note: When you push a local branch that does not have a corresponding remote branch, a remote branch with the same name is created automatically.

section.title: Pull Changes
section.p: On Git Staging, select to download commits from the remote repository and update your local branch.
The drop-down menu offers two options:

ul.li: Pull (merge) - Merges the remote commits into your local branch. Creates a merge commit if both branches have new commits.
Pull (rebase) - Replays your local commits on top of the remote commits. Keeps a linear history without merge commits.

section.p: The option you choose becomes the default action for the toolbar button.
To pull from a different remote branch, use Pull....
If the pull causes file conflicts, resolve them before continuing. For details, see .
